citation.title: Acute New Zealand blackcurrant powder and caffeine on high-intensity intermittent running (modified Loughborough Intermittent Shuttle Test), blood lactate and free fatty acids in recreationally active males

reported.what: Serum free fatty acids, PLA arm: baseline (before drink, taken at minute 29 of the run-in, just before the drink at 30) and 1 h after the drink (minute 90); mean and SD, n = 14

location.where: Table 4, row 'Free fatty acids', PLA, columns Baseline and 1 h After Study Drink

reported.what: Systolic BP (supine, Omron), PLA arm: baseline and 1 h after the study drink; mean and SD, n = 14

location.where: Table A1, row 'Systolic Blood Pressure', PLA, columns Baseline and 1 h After Consuming the Study Drink

reported.what: Diastolic BP (supine, Omron), PLA arm: baseline and 1 h after the study drink; mean and SD, n = 14

location.where: Table A1, row 'Diastolic Blood Pressure', PLA, columns Baseline and 1 h After Consuming the Study Drink

reported.what: Heart rate (supine, Omron) 1 h after the study drink, PLA arm; mean and SD, n = 14

location.where: Table A2, row 'Heart Rate', PLA, column 1 h After Drink

detail: Every value in the placebo arm (baseline and 1 h after the drink) was measured the morning after a deliberate ~90 min glycogen-depleting cycling ride the afternoon before (paper: a 88-92% estimated fall in muscle glycogen before the overnight fast), which the model cannot be told, as with eshghi-2017's day 2; the paper also gives no clock time or minutes between the baseline and the drink, and the placebo carbohydrate is maltodextrin with added fructose and glucose.
